name: BaByliss trimmers/stylers

lead: BaByliss makes hair dryers, straighteners, curling irons, clippers and beard trimmers; the brand began in France in 1960 and has been owned by Conair since 1995. Users reach for its clippers and trimmers to keep haircuts, fades, beard edges and necklines sharp and even at home.

Clippers and trimmers cut with two close-fitting blades, one moving sideways against the other, driven by a motor. The cleaner lines are visible immediately. No appearance-outcome studies exist for the brand.

paras: Users run clippers with guards for length and a trimmer for edging and outlines, usually every week or so to keep lines crisp. They are often paired with a beard routine or a regular fade.
No safety data on specific models were available. A general reference notes blades need lubrication and that ceramic blades can break. Nicks and skin irritation are possible with close trimming.

chain: Sharp, even hair and beard lines
angle.text: Users reach for BaByliss clippers and trimmers to keep haircuts, fades, beard edges and necklines tidy at home. The blades give sharper, even lines that are visible immediately, for a cleaner and more polished look.

lead: BaByliss is a French personal care brand, owned by the American group Conair since 1995, that sells hair dryers, curling irons, straighteners and, under its professional and men's lines, hair clippers and beard trimmers.[1] People use its trimmers and stylers to keep haircuts, fades, beard lines and necklines sharp at home, and the brand's professional line is aimed at salons and hairstylists.[1]

A clipper cuts with two comb-like blades, one sliding sideways against the other in a scissor-like action, driven by a magnetic, rotary or pivot motor.[2] Blades and guards set cut length, from fine zero blades that leave almost no hair to coarser blades that leave more, so one tool can produce a buzz cut, a tapered side or a clean outline around the beard and hairline.[2] A good edge and clean lines are what many people want from a trimmer: a crisp hairline and beard line frame the face and jaw.

The brand traces back to hairdressers René Lelièvre and Roger Lemoine in Montmartre, who invented the first electric hair straightener, which Jean-Pierre Feldblum marketed as BaByliss in July 1960.[1] Wikipedia notes that Arab News called it the first preference of beauty salons and hairstylists, and that it is also a major brand affected by counterfeits.[1]
infobox: France, marketed as BaByliss from July 1960[1]

paras: According to Wikipedia, hairdressers René Lelièvre and Roger Lemoine in Montmartre invented the first electric hair straightener, which Jean-Pierre Feldblum marketed under the BaByliss name in July 1960.[1] The company expanded across Western Europe, and Conair bought a majority share in February 1995; at that point about 45 percent of sales were abroad, mainly through subsidiaries in Germany, England, Belgium, the Netherlands and Spain.[1] A professional line, BaBylissPRO, and a men's grooming line launched later, with BaByliss for Men in 2003.[1]

Since 2010, BaBylissPRO has produced hair dryers with engines designed with input from Ferrari engineers, and appliances are made at several Conair plants including one in Chiuduno, Italy acquired from Coif'In in 2009.[1] Reported 2024 revenue was about 175 million euros.[1]

A general reference explains that clippers use two comb-like blades, one sliding sideways against the other, to cut hair with a scissor-like action, and that motors are of magnetic, rotary or pivot types.[2] Low blade friction, kept up by lubrication, is described as important, and ceramic blades resist corrosion and stay sharp longer but are brittle and costly to replace.[2] Blades are usually rust-resistant stainless steel.[2]
Blade numbers set the length left: fine zero blades leave the least hair, and a number 1 blade leaves about 1.6 mm, regrowing in about 3.5 days, while a number 2 leaves about 6.4 mm.[2]

Manual clippers were invented around 1855 by Serbian barber Nikola Bizumić.[2] Leo J. Wahl patented what is described as the first electric hair clipper by 1921, and Mathew Andis entered the market in the same year; John Oster joined in 1928.[2] Barbers historically used manual clippers to cut hair close and quickly.[2]

Features that differ across clippers and trimmers include blade material (stainless steel or ceramic), motor type, corded or cordless operation and the set of guards.[2] Blades need frequent lubrication, and cheaper or counterfeit versions of well-known brands are a noted issue with BaByliss.[1][2]
No studies found of BaByliss trimmers or stylers for appearance outcomes.
